categories.name: Own Your Data Science and AI Workshop
Build Your Own Agentic App Workshop

speakers.name: Ignacio Ahedo
speakers.bio:
As a Program Manager at the Eclipse Foundation, Ignacio orchestrates the Oniro Working Group alongside the IoT and Sparkplug programs. A Telecommunications Engineer and PMP with a product-led mindset, he specialises in the strategic stewardship of open source ecosystems, focusing on how vendor-neutral collaboration can solve complex fragmentation challenges in the hardware and software landscape.

Drawing on his background in IoT and connectivity strategy from his time at Vodafone Business, Ignacio helps organisations navigate the value proposition of open collaboration. He is dedicated to building the operational frameworks and messaging that allow diverse stakeholders to contribute to a unified, distributed future for the IoT and mobile industries.

speakers.name: Sajid Alam
speakers.bio:
Senior Software Engineer at QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, where I maintain and develop Kedro, an open-source Python framework for building maintainable, modular data pipelines used by thousands of data teams worldwide. I work across the full stack: Python backend, React frontend, cloud infrastructure, and AI integrations designing systems that make complex data workflows simpler and more reliable. 
I'm passionate about developer experience, architectural design, and bridging the gap between data science experimentation and production-ready software.

speakers.name: David Arturo Amor Quiroz
speakers.bio:
I did my PhD in theoretical quantum physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), followed by a postdoctoral position in the same field at École Polytechnique in France. Since 2021, I have been a core contributor to scikit-learn, serving as a member of the documentation team to ensure clear, accessible and up-to-date documentation for easier usability.  

Currently, I’m a co-founder at :probabl., a company founded by the scikit-learn creators and maintainers. In this role, I’m part of the training and certification team, where I work developing educational materials and certification programs that bridge the gap between theory and practice, helping professionals achieve internationally recognized standards in machine learning and the related good practices.

speakers.name: Rik Arends
speakers.bio: With 20+ years’ experience as a C/C++, JavaScript and more recently Rust developer, I've always been excited by using computation for visuals and audio. For this to work you need performance, and a smooth workflow enabled by the right tooling. After having everything I wanted with C except stable code I moved to JavaScript and web technologies. However, this never got to the point of being able to make fast applications that use modern CPU and GPU power. Now with Rust we have a new chance. I've been an entrepreneur my entire life building VJ software in the 00's, then web UI technology and web IDEs with Cloud9, and am now reimagining the developer workflow in Rust with Makepad. And lately how to leverage AI to write Rust and UI code.

speakers.name: Baptiste Aubertin
speakers.bio: I'm an AI/ML engineer at Lighton, where I contributed to LightonOCR, a 1B VLM model trained for OCR that reached state of the art on the OLMoOCR benchmark

speakers.name: Virgile Batto
speakers.bio: Robot Architect specializing in the optimization, design, and control of legged robots.

speakers.name: Michael Berns
speakers.bio:
With over 23 years of international experience, I operate at the intersection of Open Source AI, digital transformation, and global ecosystem development. My mission is to leverage Generative AI and emerging technologies to drive vendor-neutral innovation and ensure digital sovereignty on a global scale.

Strategic Leadership & Impact As Head of AI for the Eclipse Foundation, I champion the advancement of Open Source AI and strategic ecosystem development. By fostering community-led collaboration and transparent technology standards, I help organizations navigate the path to digital autonomy.

Previously, at PwC Deutschland, I led initiatives that positioned the firm as a global thought leader in AI. My work focused on transformative solutions recognized by Gartner and Forrester, supported by over 100 professional publications.

A Global Track Record Prior to my move to Germany in 2018, I spent 16 years in London’s high-growth tech scene with firms such as Digital Reasoning.

speakers.name: Guillaume Blaquiere
speakers.bio:
Guillaume is a Google Developer Expert on Cloud Platform since 2019 and works at Carrefour as Group Data Architect. 

Initially Java developer, and despite positions of responsibilities, he has always kept his wish to create, develop, discover and test new solutions, especially in the Cloud, the AI & genAI. He notably contributed to Python and Go open source project and libraries (Google SDK, Airflow, ADK). 

Innovation addict and Google Cloud 3x certified, writer and speaker in his free time, he’s fascinated by the serverless and genAI solution and all the "usual" problems that they solve.

speakers.name: Evgeni Burovski
speakers.bio: Evgeni's background is computational physics, where he studied exotic states of quantum matter. This line of research involves numeric simulations, which led him towards using the NumPy stack, which led him to joining the SciPy maintainer team. Currently Evgeni works on OSS sustainability at Quansight.

speakers.name: Wenzhe Cai
speakers.bio: An Embodied AI researcher, working on building an open-sourced embodied navigation foundation models.

speakers.name: Emily Chen
speakers.bio:
Emily Chen is Co-founder of Kaiyuanshe and currently serves as General Manager of Open Source Strategy and Ecosystem at Dexmal. She is a long-time open source practitioner and community leader, dedicated to advancing collaboration between China and the global open source ecosystem.
Under her leadership, Kaiyuanshe became the first Chinese Affiliate Member of the Open Source Initiative (OSI). She also initiated several influential projects, including the China Open Source Annual Report and COSCon.
Emily was a contributor to Mozilla, a GSoC mentor, and a TOC Mentor at the OpenAtom Foundation. Recently, she initiated the RoboChallenge platform and community, one of the first large scale real robot evaluation benchmarks for embodied intelligence.
With over 20 years of experience, she worked at Sun Microsystems, Oracle, and Microsoft, with expertise in open source governance, cloud computing, and embodied intelligence.

speakers.name: Hang Chen
speakers.bio: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC38 international standard registration expert, has participated in multiple national policies and planning guidelines in the open source field, and planned the first open source system in the defense field. Participated in the key research and development plan of the National Science and Technology Department, launched the Mulan open source community and China's first and only Mulan PSL v2 international open source license. Compiled "Open Source Laws, Policies and Practices (2nd Edition)", established open source industry standards, and is committed to promoting the open source and openness of AI large models.

speakers.name: Jiabei Chen
speakers.org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences & BAAI
speakers.roleOrg: Ph.D. Student, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences & BAAI
speakers.bio: Jiabei Chen is a 2nd-year Ph.D. student at the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA), advised by Prof. Kang Liu. He has published several papers in ACL, EMNLP, and NAACL. He is currently a core contributor to the OpenSeek project of BAAI, an open-source initiative focused on efficient large language model pretraining.

speakers.name: Wenjing Chu
speakers.bio:
Wenjing is the Sr. Director of Technology Strategy on Trust of AI Agents & Agentic Systems at Futurewei. He is a long time leader of open source communities currently contributing to the OpenWallet Foundation and the Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust, and was a founding member of the OpenWallet Governing Board. He chairs the AI and Human Trust (AIM) Working Group in Trust over IP (ToIP) where the specification of TEA (TSP-Enabled AI Agents), including TMCP/TA2A (running MCP and A2A over TSP)
Is being developed. He is the co-author of the Trust Spanning Protocol (TSP) specification and is an advisor to the Linux Foundation First Person Identity Project.
speakers.roleOrg: Senior Director of Technology Strategy, Futurewei Technologies

speakers.name: Sylvain Corlay
speakers.bio:
Sylvain Corlay is the founder and president of QuantStack, a company specializing in open-source software for scientific computing.

As an open-source developer, Sylvain is highly active in the free scientific computing ecosystem, particularly in the Jupyter project, as well as in the conda-forge and xtensor projects. In 2018, he was honored, along with other Jupyter leadership members, with the ACM Software System Award.

Beyond QuantStack, Sylvain is deeply involved in the community. He served on the board of directors of the NumFOCUS Foundation from 2018 to 2024, organized JupyterCon 2023 in Paris, and has coordinated the PyData community in Paris since 2017, acting as the organizer of the meetup group and the PyData conference in 2024 and 2025.

speakers.name: Sébastien Crozet
speakers.bio: Sébastien Crozet has been in love with the Rust programming language since its earliest days. He is the creator and maintainer of popular open-source libraries, including nalgebra and Rapier, for the Rust ecosystem that specialize in linear algebra, geometry, and physics. He is the founder of Dimforge where he focuses on contributing to the future of cross-platform scientific computing and AI.

speakers.name: Charbel Dandjinou
speakers.bio: Charbel is the founder and CTO of Reflexion Robotics, a Paris-based startup building A OS  - a safety runtime for embodied AI. Previously AI Research Engineer and MLOps Tech Lead at EXXACT Robotics. He also founded IROKO and the Deep Takka research lab, focused on making AI accessible and inclusive.

speakers.name: Daniel
speakers.bio: As Minimax’s European Representative, I’m driven by a deep passion for AI and a commitment to staying ahead of the curve. I constantly track the latest market trends and technological shifts across Europe, ensuring I bring you not just a product, but the most forward-thinking AI solutions available today.

speakers.name: Quentin Delfosse
speakers.bio: I am a researcher at Google, in the Intrinsic team that does AI robotics.

speakers.name: Julien Enoch
speakers.bio: Julien is an Eclipse Zenoh committer and a Senior Solutions Architect at ZettaScale Technology. He has been deeply involved in the development of Zenoh and its integration with the ROS 2 ecosystem, from the early zenoh-bridge-dds plugin to rmw_zenoh and now ros-z. Julien is a regular speaker in the open-source and robotics community — he has presented at EclipseCon (2022), ROSCon (2022 to 2025), ROSCon FR (2024, 2025), ROSCon UK (2025) and FOSDEM (2025, 2026).

speakers.name: Nicolas Flores-Herr
speakers.bio:
I am the Site Lead of Fraunhofer IAIS in Dresden, where I head an interdisciplinary team working since 2022 on the development and application of large language models (LLMs) and generative AI. Our expertise spans the full lifecycle: from dataset creation, pretraining and continued pretraining to fine-tuning and instruction tuning. We carry out this work in European flagship projects such as OpenGPT-X, TrustLLM, OpenEuroLLM and Eurolingua.

In my leadership role, I combine scientific excellence with strategic impact. My team develops bespoke GenAI solutions for industry partners across diverse sectors, including scalable enterprise chatbots and specialised tools for semantic search and knowledge access.
speakers.roleOrg: Team Lead Foundation Models, Fraunhofer IAIS

speakers.name: Thomas Froment
speakers.title: Program Manager, Development Tools, Eclipse Foundation
speakers.bio: Thomas Froment is the Program Manager for Development Tools at the Eclipse Foundation, where he oversees all tooling projects, including Eclipse Theia and Theia AI, as part of the Cloud DevTools Working Group. He also leads the Open VSX and Eclipse IDE working groups.
speakers.roleOrg: Program Manager, Development Tools, Eclipse Foundation

speakers.name: Erwan Gallen
speakers.role: Senior Principal Product Manager - Generative AI
speakers.roleOrg: Senior Principal Product Manager - Generative AI, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Erwan Gallen is Senior Principal Product Manager, Generative AI, at Red Hat, where he follows Red Hat AI Inference product and manages hardware-accelerator enablement across OpenShift, RHEL AI, and OpenShift AI. His remit covers strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle management for AI accelerators, and emerging silicon, ensuring customers can run state-of-the-art generative workloads seamlessly in hybrid clouds.

speakers.name: Olivier Grisel
speakers.bio: Olivier Grisel is a software engineer at Probabl and a core contributor of the scikit-learn project.

speakers.name: Tim Head
speakers.bio: I am a scikit-learn and cuML maintainer. I work at NVIDIA

speakers.name: Jacky Hsu
speakers.bio:
Jacky Hsu is the Founder of Ingora, an AI-native learning companion company building next-generation AI companion devices for children.

Previously, he spent over 20 years at Microsoft as a product leader, where he led product strategy and growth initiatives across multiple businesses including SharePoint Copilot and Agent. He played a key role in bringing Copilot and Agent experiences into real-world enterprise scenarios.

Jacky combines deep expertise in AI product design with a unique perspective on integrating agent systems, education, and hardware. At Ingora, he is exploring how AI companions can reshape how children learn, think, and grow.

speakers.name: Xuan Huang
speakers.bio: Xuan Huang (@huxpro) is the Architect of Lynx at ByteDance, an open-source, cross-platform framework powering TikTok and CapCut. He is exploring what app frameworks should look like in the age of AI, and he was previously on the React Core Team at Meta.

speakers.name: Zhipeng Huang
speakers.bio: Zhipeng Huang currently serve as Director of AI Open Source for Huawei. Zhipeng is now the Board chairperson of LFAI&Data Foundation, TAC Chair of Open Model Initiative, executive member of CCF Open Source Development Committee, co-lead of the Kubernetes Policy WG, project lead of CNCF Security SIG, founder of the OpenStack Cyborg project, and co-founder of OpenStack Public Cloud WG. Zhipeng used to give Keynote presentations at OpenStack Summit, KubeCon and RISC-V Workshop

speakers.name: Priyanka Jain
speakers.bio: Building non-invasive brain computer interfaces.

speakers.name: Chao Jia
speakers.bio: Chao Jia, Vice President of Technology at ModelBest and Co-founder of the OpenBMB open-source community. He is primarily responsible for organizing the R&D and open-source management of the MiniCPM series of on-device models. Dubbed the "ModelBest's Little Steel Cannon" the MiniCPM family—which includes the MiniCPM large language model and the MiniCPM-o omni-modal model—has earned widespread acclaim in the global AI community for its high efficiency, low cost, and ability to "punch above its weight." To date, these projects have amassed over 30,000 stars on GitHub and exceeded 24 million downloads worldwide, establishing themselves as benchmark works in the field of on-device AI.

speakers.name: Alexy Khrabrov
speakers.title: Founder, CR4AI; Northeastern University
speakers.bio: Alexy Khrabrov is the AI Community Architect at Neo4j, the category-defining Graph database company. Alexy is the founding Chair of Open-Source Science at NumFOCUS, and a cofounder of the AI Alliance. Alexy was the founding Chair of the Generative AI Commons at the Linux Foundation for AI and Data (LFAI) and now represents Neo4j at LFAI. Alexy is the founder and organizer of Bay Area AI and AI Agent SF meetups, as well as the Scale/Data/AI By the Bay conferences, the independent OSS AI conference running since 2013.

speakers.name: Jeremy Laville
speakers.bio: Mechanical engineer with a strong passion for robotics. Worked for Aldebaran on the Pepper robot, and more recently on Reachy 2 for Pollen Robotics. Also designed the Amazing Hand open-source project.

speakers.name: Bryce Adelstein Lelbach
speakers.bio:
Bryce Adelstein Lelbach has spent over a decade developing programming languages, compilers, and libraries. He is passionate about parallel programming and strives to make it more accessible for everyone.

Bryce is a Principal Engineer at NVIDIA, where he founded the Core C++ Compute Libraries team and now leads the Vanguard Programming group that drives NVIDIA's roadmap for programming languages, compilers, and core libraries.

He is a leader of the systems programming language community, having served as chair of the C++ Library Evolution and the US programming language standards committee. He has been an organizer and program chair for many conferences over the years. On the C++ committee, he has worked on concurrency primitives, parallel algorithms, senders, and multidimensional arrays.

Outside of work, Bryce is passionate about airplanes and watches. He lives in Midtown Manhattan with his girlfriend and dog.

speakers.name: Jianzhong Li
speakers.bio: He is currently the President of Singularity Intelligence Research Institute and Senior Vice President of CSDN, with profound insights and in-depth research experience in the fields of artificial intelligence, technological innovation and industrial ecology. He initiated and founded the Singularity Intelligence Technology Summit (SITS) in 2016, which has become a highly influential high-end technical seminar and exchange platform in the field of AI. In recent years, he has mainly focused on the AI paradigm Shifts, and his related research and speeches have attracted great attention in the industry. In 2005, he initiated and organized the 1st C++ and System Software Technology Conference, and is a member of the ISO-C++ International Standards Committee. He is also a member of the Artificial Intelligence Expert Committee of the Science Technology Vision Forum, and jointly released "Tech Predictions and Future Visions 2049'" with many scientists at Tengchong Scientists Forum in 2025.

speakers.name: Yonghua Lin
speakers.bio: Yonghua Lin is the Vice President and Chief Engineer of Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, responsible for AI System, and Large Model Foundation Technology research, industry and open-source ecosystem cooperation. She is formerly the Director of IBM China Research Lab and Distinguished Engineer at IBM, she led global AI system innovation within IBM. She has been engaged in research on system architecture, cloud computing, AI systems, computer vision, and other fields for more than 20 years. She holds over 50 global patents and has won the ACM/IEEE Best Paper awards. She was named one of the "50 Leading Female Tech Leaders in China" by Forbes in 2019. She is member of IEEE Women in Engineering Asia Pacific Leadership Team and the founder of IEEE Women in Engineering Beijing affinity.

speakers.name: Shiwei Liu
speakers.bio: Shiwei Liu is a group leader at Max Planck Institute for Intelligent System and a PI at ELLIS Institute Tubingen. He was a Royal Society Newton International Fellow at the University of Oxford. He previously served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Texas at Austin. He obtained his Ph.D. with Cum Laude from Eindhoven University of Technology in 2022. Dr. Liu has received two Rising Star Awards from KAUST and the Conference on Parsimony and Learning (CPAL). His Ph.D. thesis received the 2023 Best Dissertation Runner-up from Informatics Europe. He has a broad interests of life-cycle of large foundation models.
speakers.org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
speakers.roleOrg: Group Leader & PI, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

speakers.name: Luke Lu
speakers.bio: Luke is a student at the University of Texas at Austin and the founder of Inhabit, an open-source humanoid robot teleoperation platform. His journey in robotics began as a competitor, rising through the ranks of competitive robotics to claim a world championship title. That experience ignited a drive to mentor aspiring engineers and contribute to the open-source robotics community. Today, Luke channels that same competitive energy into founding technology ventures at the intersection of AI and robotics, believing that the best ideas should be accessible to everyone willing to build them.

speakers.name: Christian Maitre
speakers.bio:
A digital transformation and innovation expert with extensive international leadership experiences in Telecom
President & Founder – Caspera-Lab, Founder of Caspera-Lab, a premier global advisory firm specializing in guiding the telecom companies to (re) build, review, (re)start their sustainable digital transformation journeys with AI, genAI and Agentic AI.
Former CIO deputy for Digital Transformation – Orange Group, 10 years as Group CIO driving digital transformation worldwide  (21 opcos),
TM Forum partner / ambassador, Recognized contributor to TM Forum innovation programs, founder of the autonomous networks concepts, leader on digital Maturity evaluation project
Foreign Trade Advisor of France (CNCCEF), Chair of the Digital-IA-Tech Expert Group at CNCCEF a french governmental association.

speakers.name: Bart Massey
speakers.roleOrg: Assoc Prof Computer Science, Portland State University
speakers.bio: Bart Massey is a 26-year CS Professor with a PhD in AI and an MSc in PL implementation; he has been an open source developer for many decades. Bart is a member of the Rust Embedded Working Group, and is involved in a number of low-level Rust and Rust Education projects.

speakers.name: Niko Matsakis
speakers.bio: Nicholas Matsakis is a Senior Principal Engineer at AWS and co-lead of the open source Rust language design team. He has worked on Rust since 2011, and led the design of its “secret sauce”, the borrow checker. He has played a number of other roles in Rust over the years, such as being a member of the Rust core team, the lead of the Rust compiler team, and helping to launch the Rust Foundation. Prior to working on Rust, he completed a PhDat ETH Zurich and did his undergraduate study at MIT.

speakers.name: Minako Kojima
speakers.bio: I'm the Head of Developer Relations at Kimi, where I've also held positions in post-training and infrastructure. Prior to joining Kimi, I worked as an algorithm engineer at Google. I won several gold medals at ACM ICPC regional contests during college.
speakers.roleOrg: Head of Developer Relations, Moonshot AI (Kimi)

speakers.name: Tom Mulder
speakers.bio: All round builder with 27 years professional experience, 17 years in ML / AI and a lifelong passion for robotics

speakers.name: Xuan-Son Nguyen
speakers.bio: I'm software engineer at Hugging Face, core maintainer of llama.cpp

speakers.name: Ruben Ortlam
speakers.bio: Author and Maintainer of the llama.cpp Vulkan Backend

speakers.name: Caroline Pascal
speakers.bio: Caroline Pascal is a robotics engineer at Hugging Face, working on the LeRobot team. She’s become the team’s unofficial Swiss army knife, jumping across the library while focusing on expanding data modalities and models to make AI for robotics more accessible. She is also involved in the development and promotion of Reachy Mini, where she mainly focuses on the robot’s acoustic design and chips in on core media functionalities—basically making sure robots not only work, but sound good doing it.

speakers.name: Fabien Pesquerel
speakers.bio:
A researcher at heart with a passion for robust open source, Fabien is a Developer Relations Engineer at Probabl.
After studying mathematics, physics, and computer science at ENS Paris, he earned a PhD in Reinforcement Learning from INRIA Lille.
His career spans from postdoctoral research in cybersecurity to serving as an independent research engineer for the manga industry.
Today at Probabl, Fabien leverages this diverse technical background to empower the machine learning community, both academic and industrial, and support the sustainable growth of the open-source ecosystem.
A researcher turned community advocate.

speakers.name: Björn Plüster
speakers.bio: Co-Founder/CTO of ellamind - building the next generation of secure and reliable agentic AI. My focus is currently on secure agent runtimes, advanced evals and monitoring, and agent harness engineering to get AI agents to reliably solve real enterprise problems.

speakers.name: Bill Ren
speakers.bio: Chief Open Source Liaison Officer at Huawei and Board Member of CNCF.
speakers.roleOrg: Chief Open Source Liaison Officer, Huawei

speakers.name: Stefanie Senger
speakers.bio: Stefanie is an open-source developer and maintainer of scikit-learn, contributing also to related libraries. She trained and taught at LeWagon (2022–2023), interned with scikit-learn (2023), and worked at muffintech (2023) before joining probabl’s open-source team in 2024. She holds a PhD in History from the University of Potsdam (2021) and was active on Wikipedia as a writer and mentor (2011–2014).

speakers.name: Ran Shemtov
speakers.bio: Ran is a web developer with over a decade of experience building products for the web. Since 2023, he has been deeply involved in the emerging world of AI-powered applications, helping companies design and bring AI agents into production. At CopilotKit, Ran works closely with teams building real-world AI experiences, guiding them through the challenges of turning LLM prototypes into systems that serve real users.

speakers.name: Anastasia Stasenko
speakers.bio: Anastasia Stasenko is co-founder and CEO of Pleias, a Franco-German lab developing data infrastructure for frontier AI systems. Under her leadership, Pleias created Common Corpus — the largest open multilingual dataset for LLM training at over 2 trillion tokens — and leaded the SYNTH, producing open synthetic data at scale for training sovereign AI models and agentic applications. A senior associate lecturer at Sorbonne-Nouvelle University, she came to AI through digital humanities and philosophy degree at the École Normale Supérieure

speakers.name: Ethan (Yusheng) Su
speakers.bio: Member of Technical Staff at RadixArk

speakers.name: Said Taghadouini
speakers.bio: Said Taghadouini is an ML Research Engineer at LightOn, working on vision-language models and multimodal systems. He is part of the core team behind ModernBERT, leads LightOnOCR, and is an author of ArabicWeb24 and vit.cpp. His interests span multimodality, distributed training, and efficient ML systems.

speakers.name: Yu Tao
speakers.title: Chief Scientist, Huawei Central Software Institute Singapore
speakers.bio:
2017-2019: Senior Algorithm Engineer at Alibaba. Focused on multilingual text understanding and semantic matching.
2019-2025: Data Science Manager at Agoda.com. Led the development of agentic systems, including RAG frameworks, context engineering, prompt optimization platforms, and multi-agent systems. Also directed content intelligence solutions for image and text understanding, encompassing hotel image tagging, quality assessment, ranking, customer review analysis, and property characterization.
2025-Present: Chief Scientist at Huawei Central Software Institute Singapore. Driving the development of Huawei’s agentic platform, openJiuwen. Leading the core technology R&D for the openJiuwen Agent Harness SDK and the self-evolving agent algorithm. Responsible for executing Huawei’s super agent initiatives, making significant contributions to technical planning, system design, and productization.
speakers.roleOrg: Chief Scientist, Huawei Central Software Institute Singapore

speakers.name: Markus Tavenrath
speakers.bio:
Markus Tavenrath studied computer science with a focus on computer graphics at RWTH Aachen University. This academic background provided a solid foundation for his career in the technology industry.

In 2008, Markus joined NVIDIA, where he began working on real-time ray tracing on GPUs. Over the years, he has contributed to performance optimization for ray tracing, scene graphs, OpenGL, WebGL, Vulkan, and AI. His work has played a role in advancing these technologies.

Markus is also a co-founder of the Vulkan-Hpp project, which has been beneficial to the Vulkan community. His efforts have helped improve the use and implementation of Vulkan.

Recently, Markus was elected as the Chair of the ML Council at Khronos. In this role, he helps coordinate and support AI and machine learning initiatives within the Khronos group. His election to this position reflects his expertise and leadership qualities.

Markus Tavenrath is a dedicated professional whose contributions have positively impacted the technological landscape at NVIDIA and beyond.

speakers.name: Nouamane Tazi
speakers.bio: Nouamane Tazi is a Machine Learning Research Engineer at Hugging Face, specializing in training large language models. He is a co-author of SmolLM3 and The Ultra Scale Playbook, and his research spans NLP, deep learning, and scalable AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: Andy Terrel
speakers.bio: Andy is the CUDA Python Product Lead at NVIDIA. He has been a technical executive / product leader / ML Engineer with experience in several industries and an thought leader in the Python open data science community (PyData) with over 1000 citations of his academic articles. His work specializes in developing new technology from the ground up, scaling to large systems, and building a support team to operationalize products. He is a co-creator of the popular Dask distributed computing framework, the Conda package manager, and the SymPy symbolic computing library.

speakers.name: Gregory Terzian
speakers.bio: Servo browser engine maintainer

speakers.name: Xinyuan Tong
speakers.bio: SGLang Maintainer

speakers.name: Daniele Trifirò
speakers.bio: Daniele is a Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat, working on AI Inference. Daniele focuses on vLLM and Red Hat AI Inference Server, Red Hat's trusted and verified build of vLLM.

speakers.name: Gaël Varoquaux
speakers.bio: AI researcher, co-founder of scikit-learn and probabl

speakers.name: Vector Wang
speakers.bio: Gaotian (Vector) Wang is a Computer Science PhD student at Rice University. He is the creator of XLeRobot, a fully open-source, low-cost ($660) dual-arm mobile robot platform that has gained 4.8k+ GitHub stars and a global community of 6,000+ builders since its release in May 2025. XLeRobot is built on the Hugging Face LeRobot ecosystem and has been adopted by researchers, educators, and hobbyists worldwide.

speakers.name: Yanzhi Wang
speakers.bio: Yanzhi Wang is Professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Computer Science at Northeastern University, a senior member of IEEE. His research interests focus on real-time and energy-efficient deep learning and artificial intelligence systems, especially on efficient large language models and large-scale generative AI systems. His research works have been published broadly in (i) machine learning conferences such as AAAI, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICML, ICCV, ICLR, IJCAI, ECCV, KDD, ICRA, ACM MM, ICDM, etc., (ii) architecture and system conferences such as ASPLOS, ISCA, MICRO, HPCA, CCS, VLDB, PLDI, WWW, ICS, PACT, CGO, IPDPS, INFOCOM, ICDCS, DAC, ICCAD, FPGA, FCCM, ISSCC, CICC, RTAS, RTSS, etc., and (iii) IEEE and ACM transactions. His research works have been cited over 26,500 times. He has received six Best Paper Awards and another 12 Best Paper Nominations. His research work has been reported and cited by around 500 media. He has 15 academic descendents as tenure-track faculty members at University of Minnesota, University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Arizona, Michigan State University, University of Georgia, etc.

speakers.name: Xingda Wei
speakers.bio: Xingda Wei is a tenure-track Associate Professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His main research interests include improving the performance, reliability, and resource efficiency of system support for AI. He has published papers in conferences including OSDI/SOSP, Eurosys, and NSDI. He has received awards including the Eurosys 2024 Best Paper Award, 2022 Huawei OlympusMons Award, and 2021 ACM SIGOPS Dennis M. Ritchie Award. He serves on the program committees of multiple leading system conferences including OSDI, ASPLOS, NSDI, and as the program committee chair of ACM ChinaSys 2025 and the shadow program committee chair of Eurosys 2026.
speakers.roleOrg: Associate Professor, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

speakers.name: Yonghui Wu
speakers.bio: Dr. Yonghui Wu, associate professor at Fudan University, visiting scholar at Stony Brook University, and, the chair of the ICPC Asia Training Committee. He won three medals in ACM ICPC World Finals for Fudan University. His book series “Collegiate Programming Contests and Education” has been published in simplified and traditional Chinese and English: the former by respective publishers of mainland China and Taiwan, and the latter, the first book’s translation, by CRC Press. Since 2013, he has been giving lectures not only in China, but also in other countries.

speakers.name: Ervin Xie
speakers.bio: Weiyu Xie is a fifth-year Ph.D. student in the Institute for High Performance Computing, Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University. His research interests include computer systems, large language model (LLM) inference, graph computing, and databases.

speakers.name: Sean Dong
speakers.bio: 2008–2017: Technical Leader at Microsoft, working on the Microsoft Azure enterprise cloud and Dynamics 365 platform R&D. 2017–present: Technical Expert and Product Director at Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., working on the R&D of core infrastructure software including toolchains, programming languages, and IDEs. During his time at Huawei, he has served successively as Chief Technical Expert and Project Manager, working on Huawei’s mobile AI R&D tools, the company-wide AI R&D platform, the Huawei Ascend AI chip toolchain, and the HarmonyOS toolchain, among other initiatives. Since 2021, he has been responsible for the R&D of Huawei’s programming language and IDE infrastructure software, serving as Program Director. He leads the core technology R&D of proprietary and independently-controlled programming languages and IDE development tools, and has made significant contributions to the technical planning, productization, and industry adoption of domestically-developed application programming languages.
speakers.roleOrg: Program Director, Central Software Institute, Huawei

speakers.name: Yuhao Yang
speakers.bio: SGLang Developer

speakers.name: Michael Yuan
speakers.title: Maintainer / CEO, WasmEdge / Second State
speakers.bio: Dr. Michael Yuan is a maintainer of WasmEdge Runtime (a project under CNCF) and a co-founder of Second State. He is the author of 5 books on software engineering published by Addison-Wesley, Prentice-Hall, and O'Reilly. Michael is a long-time open-source developer and contributor. He had previously spoken at many industry conferences including Open Source Summit, RustLab Conference, GOSIM, and KubeCon.

speakers.name: Zhao Yun
speakers.bio: Zhao Yun is a Senior Engineer at Huawei. He completed his Ph.D. at Tsinghua University (2021–2025).

speakers.name: Yuxuan Zhang
speakers.bio: Technology Evangelist at ZhipuAI.

speakers.name: Lin Zhong
speakers.bio: Lin Zhong is Joseph C. Tsai Professor of Computer Science with Yale University. He received his B.S and M.S. from Tsinghua University and Ph.D. from Princeton University. From 2005 to 2019, he was with Rice University. At Yale, he leads the Efficient Computing Lab to make computing, communication, and interfacing more efficient and effective. He and his students received the best paper awards from ACM MobileHCI, IEEE PerCom, ACM MobiSys (3), ACM ASPLOS, IEEE QCE and NDSS. He is a recipient of the NSF CAREER Award, the Duncan Award from Rice University, the RockStar Award (2014) and Test of Time Award (2022) from ACM SIGMOBILE. He is a Fellow of IEEE and ACM. More information about his research can be found at yecl.org.
speakers.roleOrg: Professor of Computer Science, Yale University

speakers.name: Marcin Zubrzycki
speakers.bio: Software Engineer at Delinea (formerly StrongDM), currently studying Algorithmic Computer Science at Wrocław University of Science and Technology.

speakers.name: Tianyi HAN
speakers.role: Architect Solution, AI Systems & Agent Governance
speakers.roleOrg: Architect Solution, AI Systems & Agent Governance, Capgemini
speakers.bio: Tianyi Han is an Architect Solution focused on AI systems, agent governance, and decision-support tooling. His work explores how to make AI-driven systems more controllable, auditable, and reproducible through runtime policy enforcement, traceability, and replay.

speakers.name: Susanna Wong
speakers.bio: Susanna is a Staff Software Engineer passionate about all web technologies and engineering excellence in the adoption of AI. She has been a software developer with experience spanning across multiple industries, from small agile teams in big corporates to startups.

speakers.name: Jad Fayad
speakers.roleOrg: Manager of Systems & AI Engineering, Moon Surgical
speakers.bio: Jad Fayad is a Founding Engineer at Moon Surgical where he leads the AI engineering work. His work focuses on applying foundation models and agentic AI to surgical robotics. He has contributed to the development of Open-H Embodiment, the first open dataset for healthcare robotics.

speakers.name: Tiberiu Socaci
speakers.bio: Tiberiu Socaci is the CEO & Co-Founder of Makeitfuture — a leading AI and automation agency across the UK, France, Germany, and Romania. He is passionate about digital transformation and helping businesses streamline complex workflows using AI, Make.com, Airtable, n8n, and no-code solutions.

speakers.name: Zonghuan Wu
speakers.bio: Zonghuan Wu, Ph.D. is a core contributor to Octos, an open-source Rust-native Agentic OS, and lead of MoFA, an open-source agent framework for Composition AI. Previously a tech lead and architect at Huawei's US Research Lab, he spent over a decade building AI, knowledge graph, and search systems at scale.

speakers.name: David Cortes
speakers.bio: David Cortes is a software engineer at Intel, working in development of machine learning libraries for tabular data such as oneDAL and hardware-optimized scikit-learn extension. His areas of interest include numerical methods, applied statistics, and interop with the wider open-source ecosystem.

speakers.name: Violetta Mishechkina
speakers.bio: Violetta Mishechkina leads Solutions Engineering at dltHub, helping teams build AI-ready data pipelines using the open-source library dlt. With a background in ML and MLOps, she focuses on turning messy, real-world data into reliable inputs for production systems. Over the past few year, Violetta has led several workshops on AI and data engineering, sharing practical insights with data teams across industries.

speakers.name: Rémi Louf
speakers.bio: Rémi is co-founder and CEO of .txt, building the infrastructure that makes agentic AI production-ready. His bet: the bottleneck isn't model intelligence; it's making AI output reliable, predictable, and composable at scale.

speakers.name: Drummond Reed
speakers.bio: Drummond has spent over a quarter-century in Internet identity, security, privacy, and trust infrastructure. He is currently founder of the First Person Project and a Director of the First Person Cooperative. From 2021 to 2025, he was Director of Trust Services at Gen (formerly Avast) after their acquisition of Evernym, where he was Chief Trust Officer. He is co-author of the book, Self-Sovereign Identity (Manning Publications, 2021), and co-editor of the W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DID) 1.0 specification. He currently serves as Governance Lead for the Ayra Association. He is founding board member of the OpenWallet Foundation and Trust Over IP (ToIP), where he serves as co-chair of the Technology Stack Working Group, the Decentralized Trust Graph Working Group, and the Concepts and Terminology Working Group. In 2002 he received the Digital Identity Pioneer Award from Digital ID World, and in 2013 he was cited as an OASIS Distinguished Contributor.

speakers.name: Wendy Seltzer
speakers.bio:
Wendy Seltzer is a lawyer and technologist, currently consulting via the Law Office of Wendy Seltzer. She is a founder of the First Person Cooperative, addressing governance of decentralized trust networks for personhood recognition and agency.

As Principal Identity Architect at Tucows, she helped to found the Ayra Association. She previously served as Strategy Lead and Counsel to the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) at MIT, improving the Web's security, availability, and interoperability through standards. As a Fellow with Harvard's Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society, Wendy founded the Lumen Project (formerly Chilling Effects Clearinghouse), the web's pioneering transparency report to measure the impact of legal takedown demands online. She seeks to improve technology policy in support of user-driven innovation and secure communication. She co-authored the second edition of Blown to Bits: Your Life, Liberty, and Happiness After the Digital Explosion.
speakers.roleOrg: Principal, Law Office of Wendy Seltzer

speakers.name: Junyi Zhong
speakers.bio: Dr. Junyi Zhong is a tech entrepreneur and AI researcher specializing in Trustworthy AI and blockchain systems. He is the CEO of INNAIO France, he focuses on AI-driven voice interfaces to advance information accessibility and global communication. He is also an active angel investor, supporting early-stage projects across AI and Web3.

speakers.name: Eva Ma
speakers.bio: Taming the wild frontiers of generative AI. I design the structures that keep modern algorithms bounded, efficient, and aligned with human intent. Architecting the future of Atlas Cloud AI.
speakers.roleOrg: Algorithmic Tamer, Atlas Cloud AI LLC

speakers.name: Jenia Jitsev
speakers.bio: Scientific lead & chairman LAION e.V. Open foundation models & datasets (openCLIP, LAION-5B, DataComp, DCLM, OpenThoughts, MixtureVitae). Scaling laws for guided search  of stronger scalable learning procedures.

speakers.name: Marianna Nezhurina
speakers.bio: Core LAION researcher, main contributor to OpenThoughts, OpenThoughts-Agent and TerminalBench projects.

speakers.name: Mirko Boehm
speakers.bio:
Mirko Boehm contributes to free and open source software as a community builder, licensing expert and researcher. His work spans major projects including the KDE Desktop, the Open Invention Network and the Open Source Initiative. He holds a PhD in innovation economics and serves as visiting lecturer and researcher on open source software at the Technical University of Berlin. His professional background encompasses entrepreneurship, executive management, software development and service
as a German Air Force officer. Since joining the Linux Foundation in June 2023 as senior director for community development at Linux Foundation Europe, he drives engagement and collaboration among European open source stakeholders. He is fluent in English and German and resides in the Berlin area.

speakers.name: Yun Lin
speakers.bio: Associate Professor and Deputy Head of the Department of Computer Science and Technology, School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
speakers.roleOrg: Associate Professor, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

speakers.name: Debayan Roy
speakers.roleOrg: Principal Research Engineer, Huawei Hilbert Research Center (Dresden)

speakers.name: Francesco Pham
speakers.roleOrg: Senior Technical Expert, Huawei Kopernik Research Center; Project Lead & Committer Representative, Eclipse Oniro

speakers.name: Gábor Soós
speakers.bio: Gábor Soós, PhD is Advisory Committee Member of the International Centre for Creativity and Sustainable Development (ICCSD) under the auspices of UNESCO, serving in his personal capacity. His work focuses on AI, culture, education, and public-interest innovation, with particular interest in governance-first digital companions, place-based knowledge systems, and evaluation approaches for high-trust deployment contexts. He is currently Project Lead of Source2Sea: Bartók 3.0 Connectivity (2026–2031), a UN Ocean Decade Action linking cultural and water systems through community-grounded and digitally enabled approaches.
speakers.org: International Centre for Creativity and Sustainable Development (ICCSD), UNESCO

speakers.name: Qigang Zhu
speakers.bio: Zhu Qigang, Open Source Expert at Beijing Artificial Intelligence Institute and Secretary General of FlagOS Open Source Community, Deputy Director of the Global Open Source Collaboration Research Center at the University of International Business and Economics, Executive Member of the Open Source Development Committee of the China Computer Federation, former Secretary General of the Shanghai Open Source Information Technology Association, former core member of the OpenHarmony Team , former head of the Business Development Department, Education and Training Department, and Industry Research Department at the Open Atom Open Source Foundation. One of the early promoters of open source hardware and open source education in China.
speakers.roleOrg: Head of Open Source Engineering, BAAI

speakers.name: Jian Tao
speakers.bio: Researcher at the System Intelligence Group, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI), contributing to KernelGen. Focused on automated Triton operator synthesis and engineering applications, building an open-source high-performance operator ecosystem, and exploring full-process techniques from automatic generation to performance optimization and formal verification.

speakers.name: Sir Timothy Gowers
speakers.roleOrg: Professor of Combinatorics; Fields Medalist, Collège de France, Cambridge University
speakers.bio: Timothy Gowers is a mathematician. He was an undergraduate at Cambridge University, and also did a PhD there under the supervision of Béla Bollobás. This was followed by a research fellowship at Trinity College and a lectureship at University College London. In 1995 he returned to Cambridge where he has worked in various capacities ever since. In 2020 he became a professor at the Collège de France, retaining a part-time position at Cambridge. For his mathematical research he has received several prizes, including a Fields Medal in 1998. He is also the author of Mathematics: A Very Short Introduction and the main editor of The Princeton Companion to Mathematics. In 2012 he was knighted for services to mathematics.

speakers.name: Mo Sadek
speakers.bio: Mo Sadek is a Technical Director at Alice, where he spends most of his time thinking about how AI systems fail in creative and unfortunate ways. His background runs from pentesting to building security programs at platform scale, with a judgmental cat and a board game losing streak he refuses to acknowledge.

speakers.name: Mike Basios
speakers.bio: Mike Basios is Co-Founder and CTO of TurinTech AI, a London-based AI company pioneering automated code optimisation. He leads the development of Artemis, an agentic platform that uses evolutionary algorithms and multi-LLM orchestration to optimise software for performance, cost, and correctness — deployed by leading hardware vendors, financial institutions, and enterprises focused on improving the quality and performance of their code. A UCL PhD graduate, Mike has authored peer-reviewed papers on evolutionary software optimisation and is a recipient of the ACM GECCO Human-Competitive Results Award.

speakers.name: Tricia Wang
speakers.bio: Tricia Wang is a globally recognized technology and strategy expert at the intersection of AI, data, and human insight. She is the co-founder and CEO of the Advanced AI Society, an industry association for companies building AI with demonstrable, verifiable control over what their systems do. Learn more at triciawang.com.

speakers.name: Hao Li
speakers.bio: Dr. Hao Li is a Franco-Chinese entrepreneur who previously held AI leadership roles at IBM, Sodexo, and Capgemini Invent, advising CAC40 companies and public institutions. He is now founder of Haoeasy AI SAS, building multi-agent systems for enterprise transformation.

speakers.name: Nowa Sutaka
speakers.bio: CEO/Founder of Puddin AI

speakers.name: Quentin Feuillade-Montixi
speakers.bio: Ex world class AI red teamer and AI safety researcher, now creating a new programming system for the future of intelligent software.

speakers.name: Nicolas Miailhe
speakers.bio: Nicolas (Nico) Miailhe is a recognized pioneer of global AI policy and governance. He co-founded AI Safety Connect (AISC), a multi-stakeholder convening platform that advances international coordination on the safety of advanced AI systems. Nico is also the co-founder and CEO of PRISM Eval, a Paris-based frontier AI safety start-up specializing in evaluations and interpretability. For the decade prior, he founded and ran The Future Society (TFS), one of the first independent AI policy think tanks that he started at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government in 2014. Nico is an appointed expert to APEC/PECC, UNESCO, OECD, GPAI, the UN, and others, and has held teaching positions at Sciences Po and IE University. Nico holds degrees from Harvard Kennedy School, Paris-Panthéon-Assas, and Sciences Po Strasbourg.

speakers.name: Igor Schwarzmann
speakers.bio: Strategic advisor at the intersection of culture and technology. 20 years of experience across Health, Automotive, Luxury, Media, and Government, working with global technology companies, European multinationals, and institutions in the US, Europe, China, and Singapore. Hosts Follow the Rabbit, a podcast on cultural phenomena. Powered by his own agentic AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: Slava Tykhonov
speakers.bio: Head of AI at CODATA, working on Semantic Croissant and the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) for Agentic AI.

speakers.name: Tianyi Han
speakers.role: Architect Solution, AI Systems & Agent Governance
speakers.roleOrg: Architect Solution, AI Systems & Agent Governance, Capgemini
speakers.bio: Tianyi Han is an Architect Solution focused on AI systems, agent governance, and decision-support tooling. His work explores how to make AI-driven systems more controllable, auditable, and reproducible through runtime policy enforcement, traceability, and replay. He is currently building systems that bridge the gap between experimental LLM applications and production-grade AI infrastructure, with a focus on governance, observability, and reliable execution.

speakers.name: Hai-Xu Cheng
speakers.bio: Hai-Xu Cheng currently works as the CTO (Chief Technology Officer) of Rothwell International after he retired from the role of IBM Global Lead and IBM GCG CTO of standards and open source. Hai-Xu's current major focus is providing consulting services for enterprise clients at C-level on architectures, standards and open source. In his prior role at IBM, Hai-Xu led the IBM global & China teams working to develop open source communities and technologies that span AI, data & analytics, cloud computing, quantum computing, & blockchain etc & advocated the clients adopting the open technologies to fuel innovation in both technical and business domains. Hai-Xu has personally involved in the development of many China standards at CCSA (ICT), TC260 (Cybersecurity), TC28 (SC38 (Cloud), SC42(AI)), and international standards at ISO/IEC JTC1 SC42 (AI), SC38 (Cloud), & ISO TC307 (Blockchain). Hai-Xu has also actively engaged in developer advocacy, open source projects promotion & ecosystem dev.

speakers.name: Joanna Kramer
speakers.bio: Currently based in Paris, Joanna's career has blended industry and research. After earning her MSc from University of Oxford's Internet Institute, where she studied the breakdown of digital platforms and the creation of digital 'ruins,' she co-founded WISE with Michelle Nie and Nitya Kuthiala to build community and foster connections among women working across AI safety, ethics, and governance; one year later, the network has expanded to 5 WISE chapters across Brussels, Delhi, London, Paris, and Washington, D.C. In addition, Joanna leads market research and technical marketing initiatives at an applied AI research lab.

speakers.name: Adam Barker
speakers.roleOrg: Director of Systems Infrastructure Research (SIR), Huawei

speakers.name: Bart Kubiak
speakers.bio:
Bartosz Kubiak is an AI governance strategist and ERA:AI Fellow whose work sits at the intersection of frontier AI policy and physical compute infrastructure. He holds an MPP from the Oxford University’s Blavatnik School of Government and has spent a decade advising governments and Fortune 100 technology firms on EU regulatory strategy.

Most recently, he structured a €25 billion AI Gigafactories public-private partnership framework for the European Commission — one of the EU’s flagship initiatives to build sovereign compute capacity at scale. His research focuses on legal personhood frameworks for autonomous AI agents, exploring how governance structures can keep pace with agentic systems.

Previously, as Head of the Warsaw Office at the Aspen Institute, he convened C-suite leaders from Intel, Amazon, and Microsoft on transatlantic digital infrastructure policy. He teaches AI governance at BlueDot Impact. ISF Fellow. Graduate of Law with American Law LLB from the University of East An
speakers.org: New Intelligence Centre for Empathy and Reason
speakers.roleOrg: Co-Founder, New Intelligence Centre for Empathy and Reason

speakers.name: Fraser Edwards
speakers.bio: Fraser Edwards (CEO) co-founded cheqd, led WEF's Known Traveller Digital Identity pilot, and holds patents in cross-ledger cryptography.

speakers.name: Pierre-Yves Gibello
speakers.bio:
Pierre-Yves, originally a software development engineer, is the CEO of OW2 since 2022: a European non-profit FOSS foundation, we host open source projects, promote them, animate a community mixing academics, companies, public bodies, foundations, associations and individuals, promote FOSS by organizing or participating to professional events,
and advocate for it at political and social levels. OW2 is also involved in the NGI and Open Internet Stack EU FOSS funding programmes.

speakers.name: Sizhe Cheng
speakers.bio: Chengsizhe is a software engineer and independent game developer building multi-agent systems and strategy games, with years of experience in the game industry.

speakers.name: Xiaolu Tan
speakers.bio: Xiaolu Tan received his PhD from Ecole Polytechnique in Paris in 2011. He became then assistant professor at University of Paris-Dauphine, PSL university, and later moved to the Chinese University of Hong Kong where he is currently a full professor. His research focuses on stochastic optimal control, optimal transport with applications in machine learning, finance, etc.
speakers.org: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
speakers.roleOrg: Professor, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

speakers.name: Alexandre Gerbeaux
speakers.bio:
Alexandre Gerbeaux is a global AI leader operating at the intersection of advanced machine learning, enterprise strategy, and real-world impact. As Head of Applied AI at Fundamental, he is focused on turning frontier AI research into production systems for enterprise customers.

With a career spanning leadership roles at Mistral AI and DataRobot, Alexandre has built and led high-performing AI teams across different markets, working with organizations across finance, insurance, and healthcare to unlock value from data. His experience ranges from hands-on data science to executive-level AI strategy, giving him a uniquely holistic perspective on the field.

Alexandre's work is grounded in both technical depth and business relevance — covering machine learning, big data systems, and quantitative finance — while always focusing on delivering practical outcomes with measurable impact.

speakers.name: Chenzhe Jing
speakers.bio: Director of Modelbest OSPO and OpenBMB Operation Lead. Chenzhe focuses on on-device large models including MiniCPM and MiniCPM-o, and their real-world applications across smart cockpits, smartphones, smart home devices, and robotics.
speakers.role: Director of Modelbest OSPO, OpenBMB Operation Lead
speakers.roleOrg: Director of Modelbest OSPO, OpenBMB Operation Lead
